To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SENTINEL-2 mission will be the first space mission to be equipped by a large format CMOS detector.

the SENTINEL-2 imager, which is based on a 0. 35μm CIS foundry process, is the first space application to benefit from the combination of a low KTC noise readout mode, an output voltage swing optimised for the dynamic range, a conversion gain control and RTS noise reduction.
CMOS image sensor can be successfully used for space application.

the development of a CMOS imager for the Sentinel 2 mission.
CMOS Image sensor processes and their application to space applications.
CMOS detector design for space applications.

CMOS foundry is a good solution to produce high performance CMOS image sensors, provided that specific R&D programs are performed to address the specific issues of each mission.
CMOS technology has been proven to be a very powerful and reliable tool for space applications.
the use of CIS processes for space applications is now possible and that it is the most promising solution for the next generation of space imaging sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CMOS foundry processes can be adapted for space applications.
a high performance CMOS imager has been developed for a large space program.
CMOS foundry can be a very attractive solution to develop space imagers, provided that specific design work has been achieved to address space mission requirements.

the use of a large volume foundry allows a significant reduction of development cost and time.

the use of CIS processes for space applications requires a specific research and development work in order to achieve specific detector performance issues such as dynamic range improvement through conversion gain optimisation.
